title: Cargo Compartment Lining Change to Flame Penetration Resistant Laminate

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Replacement of the glass reinforced cargo compartment lining by a laminate qualified to the revised burnthrough standard, closing a gap between the original certification basis and the rule now applied to Class C compartments.

sections.reason: A revision to the flame penetration requirement for Class C cargo compartment liners was adopted while the aircraft was in service. The original lining met the standard in force at type certification but not the revised one, and several authorities signalled that they would not accept the earlier qualification on aircraft entering their registers after 2022. Separately, in-service sampling showed that panels in the aft compartment lost roughly 15 per cent of their burnthrough margin over ten years of loading damage and repair, which narrowed the margin further.
sections.description: All lining panels in the forward, aft and bulk compartments are replaced by panels of a phenolic laminate with a ceramic veil on the fire side, qualified to the revised burnthrough standard with margin for in-service degradation. The decor panel D2550136675057 and the restraint lining at the aft bulkhead are replaced together, since the joint between them is the weakest point of the assembly. The upper decor panel at the compartment ceiling is attached with anchor nuts EN513769-76 to a revised pitch, and the seat track cover FIN 12DL at the bulk compartment loading floor is renewed because the new panel is thicker. The obsolete curtain rail kit D2550005854497 is deleted where fitted. Panel edge sealing uses an intumescent tape at every joint. Work is done in zones 113, 131, 143 and 973, and the compartment lighting assembly D2550007254418 is removed and refitted unchanged.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 96 kg per aircraft on a full three-compartment installation, the largest single contributor being the aft compartment ceiling. The centre-of-gravity shift is 0.11 per cent mean aerodynamic chord aft and must be recorded in the weight and balance manual. No electrical load change. The new panels are not interchangeable with the original because the thickness differs at the joint, and a compartment must be converted in full. Smoke detection sampling performance was re-tested and is unchanged. Illustrated parts content and the lining panel removal task both require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN T00179 in August 2021. In service the change is a base maintenance task of about twelve days for all three compartments, normally split across two visits so that an operator can convert the aft compartment first. Kits are supplied per compartment.

type_data.balance_impact: 0.11 % MAC aft; weight and balance manual entry required
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00179; lining kits pre-assembled off line and fitted at the same station
